free_tier.stated: No fee. A self-run bot: magnet, hash or .torrent in, selected files out into the chat. Requires a Telegram bot token and, for the full path, a local Bot API server.

per_object_cap.stated: Files above 1.9 GB are split into 7-Zip volumes because 'the self-hosted Bot API server limit is 2 GB per file'.
per_object_cap.notes: 1.9 GB is the project's own safety margin under the 2 GB ceiling

retention.stated: Whatever the chat keeps; the project caches by Telegram file_id so a repeat request re-sends instead of re-downloading.

egress.terms: Telegram's; the bot's host carries the swarm traffic and the upload.

interface_detail: A Telegram chat in front of TorrServer, plus a CLI-style configuration; lossless FLAC needs a second, user-account (MTProto) session because the Bot API only accepts .mp3/.m4a audio.
tooling: Docker or source, TorrServer, and the tdlib Bot API server for the >50 MB path; 7-Zip is mandatory for objects above 1.9 GB.
chaining: The reference implementation of the whole lane: a torrent leeched on somebody else's VM, uploaded to Telegram through a local Bot API server, split at 1.9 GB, and re-sent by file_id on request.

limits.value: 1.9 GB split threshold under the 2 GB local Bot API limit
50 MB without a local Bot API server

binding_note: The project documents the sequence exactly: 50 MB without a local server, 2 GB with one, and a 1.9 GB split above that. Nothing about flood control appears, because at these object counts it does not bind.

identity_cost.detail: api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org, hence a phone-registered Telegram account, plus a host to run TorrServer and the Bot API server.

reliability_note: A ban risk the project acknowledges in its own README; a self-run stack also means the Bot API server must be moved with logOut or updates are lost.
confidence_note: The 50 MB / 2 GB / 1.9 GB progression is stated in the project's README read today. Nothing was built.

evidence.proved: 'files larger than 1.9 GB are automatically split into 7-Zip volumes (the self-hosted Bot API server limit is 2 GB per file)'
'without it Telegram cuts file uploads to 50 MB, with it the limit is 2 GB'
for lossless FLAC a second Telegram account ('userbot', via MTProto) is used because the Bot API only accepts .mp3/.m4a for sendAudio

notes: Software, not hosted. It is the only source found that states the 50 MB -> 2 GB -> 1.9 GB-split chain in one place, which makes it the best independent confirmation of the platform caps. Abandon if the README's limit table changes.
